title: Lantern and Compass
premise: In 1899, Mirabel Marchetti, daughter of a pearl diver and indentured bookkeeper to the Halcyon Trading Company in a cyclone-battered port town, discovers a sealed company letter naming her family in a scheme to seize the lagoon's pearl beds by dispossessing its divers. Torn between the company that owns her contract and the found family of divers, smugglers, and a lighthouse keeper's son who raised her, she smuggles the letter out and spends the monsoon season forging an escape. When the century turns and a single berth on the last ship out goes unclaimed, Mirabel must decide whether to give it to her ailing father, her chosen brother, or herself — and her choice, to surrender the berth and stay to testify, breaks the company's hold and wins the divers their beds.
about_author: Freya Thackeray is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing trading-company ledgers in colonial port archives. She writes historical fiction about the people the ledgers counted but never named.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She balances the Halcyon Company's ledgers while her father's diving cough worsens, measuring her life in portable things. When a clerk burns a suspicious letter, she salvages a scrap naming 'the Marchetti family' in a land scheme. Beat: quiet dread beneath routine.

chapters.title: Indentured
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She reconstructs the letter's context from ledger entries, learning the company plans to void divers' leases on the pearl beds. Her father dismisses her fears; her found family of dockworkers urges caution. Beat: the loneliness of knowing something no one believes.

chapters.title: The Lighthouse Keeper's Son
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias, who has loved Mirabel since childhood, spots company surveyors charting the lagoon at night. He warns the divers, earning the company's enmity. Beat: love expressed as vigilance, the first open act of defiance.

chapters.title: A Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The company manager, Mr. Corvane, offers to buy out her indenture early — if she signs an affidavit denying the letter exists. She stalls, realizing he knows she saw it. Beat: the trap closing, duty weaponized against her.

chapters.title: Salt and Ink
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She begins copying evidence — lease papers, the letter fragment, diver rosters — hiding pages inside her father's diving journal. Her chosen brother, the smuggler Tomás, offers to move them by boat. Beat: purpose hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Monsoon Arrives
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Storm season strands the divers and halts the company's ships, a temporary reprieve. Elias and Mirabel repair the lighthouse together and admit what they mean to each other. Beat: stolen tenderness before the storm of consequences.

chapters.title: What the Company Owes
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Corvane, unable to buy her silence, threatens to extend her indenture and blacklist her father. Mirabel's father, proud and failing, forbids her to fight. Beat: filial duty colliding with justice.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Price
chapters.summary: Tomás's POV. Tomás agrees to carry the evidence to a colonial magistrate in the capital, but demands the family flee with him when the monsoon ends. Mirabel cannot promise. Beat: found family fracturing over what survival requires.

chapters.title: Night Chart
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias discovers the company has bribed the harbor master to control every berth on the last ship of the year. One berth will be unclaimed — reserved, he suspects, for whoever Corvane chooses. Beat: the stakes become literal and finite.

chapters.title: The Diver's Lungs
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Her father collapses; the diving cough is consumption. The doctor says he cannot survive another season here. For the first time, the berth question has a face. Beat: love made urgent by mortality.

chapters.title: Corvane's Offer
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Corvane offers the reserved berth to Mirabel herself: leave quietly, sign the affidavit, and her father keeps working. She pretends to consider, buying time. Beat: temptation wearing the mask of mercy.

chapters.title: The Journal Goes East
chapters.summary: Tomás's POV. Tomás sails for the capital with the evidence through the tail of the monsoon, nearly boarded by company agents. Beat: the found family's fate placed in one pair of hands, terror on open water.

chapters.title: Waiting Water
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. With Tomás gone, Corvane tightens the screws — divers' rations cut, leases suspended. The community looks to Mirabel, the girl with the ledgers, for a plan she doesn't have. Beat: the burden of being the one who knows.

chapters.title: What Elias Saw
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias intercepts a company telegram: the magistrate has the evidence, but Corvane has wired investors to accelerate the dispossession before any ruling. Time has run out. Beat: despair sharpening into decision.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Mirabel confronts the arithmetic she has dreaded: one berth, her dying father, Tomás returning, Elias bound to his lighthouse. She secretly secures the berth in her father's name. Beat: the choice made, and the guilt of choosing alone.

chapters.title: Betrayal or Mercy
chapters.summary: Tomás's POV. Tomás returns with a magistrate's summons for Corvane — and learns Mirabel took the berth without telling him. He accuses her of becoming the company: deciding other people's fates in secret. Beat: the found family's worst wound.

chapters.title: The Century Turns
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. On New Year's Eve, with the summons in hand and the ship at dock, Mirabel stands before her father and the berth ticket. He refuses it — he will not leave while she stays to fight. Beat: the climax of inheritance, a father giving his daughter back her choice.

chapters.title: Hearing at the Harbor House
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Mirabel testifies, reading the company's own ledgers aloud to the magistrate, her bookkeeping turned into a weapon against the men who taught it to her. Corvane's scheme unravels in his own columns. Beat: triumph earned through exposure, not escape.

chapters.title: The Cost of Staying
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. The company's agents retaliate — a fire at the lighthouse, divers arrested. Elias and the community hold the line while the magistrate's ruling lands: the leases stand, Corvane is recalled. Beat: victory with blood on it.

chapters.title: What Cannot Be Carried
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Mirabel burns her indenture contract, legally voided, and sits with her father as the monsoon ends. Some debts, she writes in the ledger, are paid in staying. Beat: grief and peace entwined.

chapters.title: The Lighthouse and the Ledger
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Spring: the divers' cooperative opens its own counting house and asks Mirabel to keep its books — her choice, her wage, her name on the door. She and Elias, rebuilding the lighthouse, choose each other plainly. Beat: love against duty resolved into love as duty freely taken.

chapters.title: Lantern and Compass
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Years later, Mirabel teaches her father's granddaughter to dive and to keep accounts, the old company letter framed as a warning on the wall. The last berth, she tells her, is the one you make yourself. Beat: inheritance redefined — what we pass on is not what we carry, but what we build.
